title: KV prefetch scheduler + lease policy sketch
content:
Summary:
This is a rough sketch for combining scheduler admission control with proactive KV-cache prefetch and a lease/slot reservation policy. The goal is to reduce tail latency for workloads that benefit from KV reuse while bounding multi-tenant interference and cost. This doc mixes heuristics, microbench experiments to run, and an outline for a prototype implementation.

Goal / non-goals:
- Goal: Keep 99.9th percentile token latency low for interactive workloads while preserving throughput economics for batchy workloads.
- Goal: Provide per-tenant configurable time budgets and soft guarantees via leases (not hard throttles).
- Non-goal: Replace token-bucket rate limiting for simple rate controls. This is an admission layer that understands kernel cost profiles + KV reuse.

Motivating observations (empirical):
- Models with large KV caches (long context + retrieval) get large wins from reusing cached KV during prefix-heavy workloads (chat with system prompts, instruction preambles).
- Prefetching KV for likely next-turn sequences reduces CPU/GPU stalls but increases memory pressure and can evict other tenants' cached states.
- Kernel execution time varies nonlinearly with input length, attention pattern, and quantization path. A single request can shift a GPU from cheap fast kernels to slower fused-kernels for a long sequence.

Key concepts / vocabulary:
- Lease: a time-limited reservation of scheduler "slot credit" + an optional KV prefetch budget. Leases are per-request-group (tenant/session) and can be reusable for short-lived chat sessions.
- Slot: a unit of GPU concurrency (soft). Allocating N slots limits concurrent active KV-holding contexts.
- Prefetch budget: bytes or number of KV rows we are allowed to populate proactively for this lease.
- Kernel class: a coarse label for execution path (e.g., short-atten, long-atten, fused-attn-quant). Used for cost estimation.

High-level design:
1) Admission entry: request arrives with metadata: tenant_id, session_id (optional), prompt_hash, expected_generation_length_hint (optional), priority, and an explicit prefetch_hint (boolean/bytes).
2) Cost estimation: lightweight estimator uses prompt_hash + length_hint + model profile to select kernel class and estimate token cost (cpu/gpu time, memory footprint, KV footprint). Estimator is best-effort and should be cheap (cache results per prompt_hash).
3) Lease decision: scheduler consults tenant quotas and current system load and either:
   - Grant a lease with slot_count=1..k, lease_ttl=ms, prefetch_budget=B;
   - Grant a deferred lease (place in soft queue with expected grant ETA); or
   - Reject/Apply immediate fallback (lower-cost model variant or throttled path).
4) Prefetch stage (optional): when lease granted and prefetch_budget>0 scheduler will schedule a prefetch job to materialize KV into local GPU memory or warm GL cache. Prefetches are prioritized by likely-reuse score (session affinity, short time-since-last-access).
5) Execution: when actual generation begins, the request will either hit warmed KV (fast path) or suffer cache miss and pay additional overhead. Lease preemption rules decide whether to evict or retain KV between leases.
6) Lease expiration/renewal: if session continues and reuse observed, lease can be renewed with adaptive backoff. If tenant exceeds soft SLOs, scheduler reduces renewals or drops prefetch budgets.

Admission policies to consider:
- Fair-share leases: maintain per-tenant moving-window credit. Each lease reduces the credit by cost_estimate. When credit low, only low-priority or fallback variants allowed.
- Hierarchical queues: sessions within a tenant can get session-priority but bounded by tenant top-level credits.
- Time-windowed quotas: measure recent served token-weighted time; convert to slot-credits for simple arithmetic.

Kernel-aware heuristics:
- When estimator classifies request as long-kernel, prefer to avoid prefetching other tenants' KV at same moment; schedule long-kernel requests on dedicated slots or low-packing bins.
- Prefer GPU locality: if a tenant already has KV resident on node X, prefer routing to X (if capacity), much like cache affinity.
- For mixed workloads, allow small short-kernel queries to opportunistically share slots with a long-kernel in background if time budgets allow (background co-packing).

KV prefetch strategy:
- Warm-up score: score = session_affinity * recency_factor * expected_length_gain. Only prefetch if score > threshold and prefetch_budget permits.
- Eviction policy: use tenant-weighted LRU with pinned reservations for active leases. Evicted entries increment a tenant eviction metric to drive future admission decisions.
- Shared prefetch pool: allow small amount of shared KV memory for opportunistic reuse across tenants, subject to global pressure signal.

Backpressure signals & telemetry:
- Node pressure levels: nominal, stretchy, congested. Determined by GPU mem usage, queued requests, and kernel queue depth.
- Advertise to clients: estimated_grant_eta ms, lease_state (granted|queued|rejected), suggested_fallback_model. Useful for SDK to surface to product teams.
- Important metrics: (per-tenant) lease_grants, lease_rejects, prefetch_hits, prefetch_misses, eviction_count, renewals, denied_due_to_kernel_long. Also node-level: active_slots, avg_slot_util, tail_latency_95/99/999.

Prototype implementation path:
- Phase 0: instrumentation-only. Log prompt_hash -> kernel_class mapping, KV hit/miss delta, and tenant->node affinity. Run offline analysis to tune estimator features.
- Phase 1: soft leases + greedy prefetch. Implement single-node scheduler that grants lease or queues. No cross-node affinity yet. Add metrics.
- Phase 2: distributed lease bookkeeping + preference routing. Add eviction counters and shared prefetch pool. Implement adaptive renewal.
- Phase 3: integrate with routing layer and fallback model variants, add SDK hooks to surface ETA and fallback hints.

Microbench experiments to run:
- Controlled sessions: measure token latency improvement vs. memory overhead for prefetch_budget in {0, 32KB, 128KB, 512KB} for a 3B/7B/13B family.
- Kernel mix stress: synthetic mix of short/long sequences to surface scheduling pathology (e.g., long kernels causing many short requests to queue). Measure tail latencies and eviction counts under different admission heuristics.
- Affinity vs. freshness: compare preference routing hit-rate vs increased cross-node load.

Open questions / risks:
- How to set lease_ttl defaults? Session length is variable. Conservative default might hurt UX.
- Billing and cost visibility: prefetching uses memory and GPU time — should be billable as separate line item for enterprise tenants?
- Security/isolation: pinned KV can contain user data; longer retention increases blast radius for co-tenancy. Need compliance guardrails.
- Complexity vs. benefit: this system increases scheduler complexity; must ensure observability and simple fallbacks.

Short TODOs:
- [ ] Add lightweight prompt_hash extractor to front-door to aid estimator caching. (Daniel)
- [ ] Run Phase 0 tracing across 2 nodes for 24 hours; produce hit/miss heatmap. (Sofia)
- [ ] Implement a toy in-memory lease manager for single node and run microbench. (Luca)
- [ ] Draft SDK ETA surface design and recommended fallback UX. (Aisha)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could consider ephemeral "micro-leases" that last only for the next generation token to enable very cheap reuse with bounded memory exposure.
- Implicit prefetch from predicted next prompts using a small next-token model (privacy implications) — interesting but likely out-of-scope.
- Maybe combine with existing token-bucket so that leases are a higher-level policy that doesn't replace low-level rate limits.

References and links:
- GitHub PR with kernel cost trace tooling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- Related tickets: ENG-1274 (kv-affinity), ENG-1302 (lease-manager), CONFLUENCE-ICU-KV-IDENT

End.
